shape: one application, one fixed service, one grading estate
why: The Angular-to-Svelte migration case study. One variable moves: the application is converted, the backend is not, and the grading suites live here rather than in the thing they grade.
ownerNote: Where a member is obtained from. Each repo resolves to `<owner>/<name>` unless it carries its own `source`. Added 2026-09-17: the descriptor named its members and never said where they live, so `repo.parseTarget` had no target and `layOutEstate` could not be implemented at all. Declared here rather than derived from the run, because an estate that only resolves when the run happens to belong to the same owner is an estate that works by coincidence.

repos.name: todo-estate
repos.role: the estate descriptor, its compose and the grading suites

repos.name: todo-backend-java
repos.role: the fixed service, which a conversion must not change

gradingSuites.note: Declared as the suite ROOT, not as the spec file. It is a Cypress project rooted here; `spec` names the file within it. Declaring the file made the hold-out manifest end in `persistence.cy.js`, so a conversion copy carrying `conformance/` under any other filename read CLEAN — a hole in the one control that protects the whole eval, opened by the declaration rather than by the code that reads it.

convertedApp.proven: 2026-09-17: the three server-persistence checks ran green against web-converted with the app served at examples/svelte/dist, pointed there by CYPRESS_baseUrl and CYPRESS_app alone and with the suites unedited. The build served was the ANGULAR one — so this proves the plumbing and the "only CYPRESS_app changes" claim, not that Svelte works. That is what a conversion has yet to earn.

measurement.why: The suites print for a person and write JUnit for a factory. Neither did until 2026-09-17: Cypress had no reporter and the contract suite printed only, so a run measuring a baseline collected zero cases and refused — honestly, and forever. `profile` is declared because a suite-to-service map would be wrong by construction here: three suites, two services.
